serializedLocalizedConversation.mainText: You: What’s your favorite animal we’ve seen so far? Bot: There’s a lot to choose from. It’s my first time seeing them in person so they are all incredible in their own right. Bot: I think turtles surprised me the most. They swim so smoothly. The difference between what they can do on land and in the water is so big! Bot: I’m also impressed with this sunfish. You: Sunfish? Of all animals to choose that one… Bot: They just drift around and are pretty much useless and yet they survived for millions of years…{{wi}} Kinda like humans! You: You can’t be serious… To be compared to sunfish of all things… You: Don’t you think you take us a little too lightly? Bot: I know, I know. Humans had some great individuals who pushed their species forward, but most of the people are just drifting around just like sunfish. Bot: And just like sunfish, out of the millions of eggs they lay, only a few ever reach their full potential. You: You sure are harsh on my people… Bot: Don’t take it too personally, I’m only half-joking. That half wasn’t necessary… Bot: And what’s your favorite animal here? You: I will go with the classic. Sharks. You: They are hundreds of millions of years old and they are still apex predators in plenty of places. Their consistency is impressive. Bot: In the recent millions of years they started losing to mammals like orcas, but they still hold their own. Bot: Most of the people think their success is mostly thanks to sharp teeth and strong bodies, but hundreds of species had that and became extinct anyway. Bot: What’s truly impressive about sharks are their sensory organs. They are able to detect electrical fields and smell blood from a great distance. #bot.Expression.VeryHappy You: I’m more of a sharp teeth and strong bodies type of guy to be honest. Bot: That’s just so like you. You: I can’t help it! They are a big part of pop culture. Sorry, but a man-eating orca will never be as scary as a man-eating shark. Bot: They just need to make more horror movies about orcas and I’m sure the trend will change. You: Maybe you are right, but orcas are still mammals so at the end of the day they are just big water puppies. Bot: It seems like mammals like to stick together. You: That may be the case. You: Let’s go explore further.
